title: Spotify Notches 300 Million Premium Subscribers
description: Spotify‘s Premium customers grew to 300 million in the second quarter of 2026, after the music streamer gained 7 million paying subscribers, exceedi
body:
Spotify‘s Premium customers grew to 300 million in the second quarter of 2026, after the music streamer gained 7 million paying subscribers, exceeding its previous guidance.

	Total monthly active users, including those on the free, ad-supported tier, stood at 777 million as of the end of Q2. That slightly undershot previous guidance of 778 million, which the company attributed to ongoing “product optimizations” in the quarter.


	For Q2, the company reported revenue of €4.78 billion, up 14% and in line with its forecast. Operating income came in at €655 million and gross margin hit an all-time high of 33.4% (above previous guidance of €630 million and 33.1%, respectively). Net income was €545 million, compared with a net loss of -€86 million in the year-ago period.
	

	Subscription revenue in the quarter grew 15% to €4.33 billion, while ad revenue inched up 1% to €446 million. Spotify said the improvement in gross margin in Q2 was driven by Premium gains (as revenue growth outpaced music costs net of marketplace programs, audiobooks costs and video podcast costs). On the ad-supported side, gains were driven by “favorable podcast and tax impacts, which more than offset music costs” and other costs of revenue.

	For Q3, Spotify expects revenue of €5.0 billion, operating income of €670 million and gross margin of 32.9%. It projects Premium subscribers of 305 million and total monthly active users of 788 million (implying the addition of approximately 11 million net new MAUs in the quarter).

	Spotify called out the launch of new initiatives in Q2 including Reserved in the U.S., which gives an artist’s most dedicated fans exclusive early access to concert tickets, and Personal Podcasts, letting users generate personalized AI-powered audio episodes.
	

	On Tuesday alongside the Q2 earnings results, Spotify announced a new agreement with Merlin for Spotify’s upcoming fan-made covers and remixing tool, which gives artists on labels under Merlin’s Spotify agreement the option to participate. As previously announced, Spotify’s tool will launch as a paid add-on, which “will create an additional revenue stream for participating artists,” the streamer said.

	Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström said in announcing the results, “We have a scale that few companies in history have reached, a business that is healthy and compounding, and opportunities only we are positioned to pursue. Spotify lives across your whole day — the commute, the workout, studying, gaming, the dinner table, and sleep. At our scale, that is rare… Our position gives us an opportunity space as wide as our users want it to be.”

	Co-CEO Gustav Söderström added, “This quarter demonstrated that we are already building that future: better engineering, faster shipping, new products and new ways for users to engage. We are still in the very early stages of what is possible and will continue to have a high bar for investments… Our job remains the same: understand the technology early and deeply, and turn it into something people love. Creating value for our stakeholders.”

title: ‘Gagarine’ Directors Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh Talk ‘The Green Eyes’ as Kinology Announces First Sales: ‘Dreamers Know No Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Having boarded as the sales agent of Locarno Film Festival‘s “The Green Eyes,” Kinology has pre-sold “The Green Eyes” to Benelux (Cinart), Switzerla
body:
Having boarded as the sales agent of Locarno Film Festival‘s “The Green Eyes,” Kinology has pre-sold “The Green Eyes” to Benelux (Cinart), Switzerland (Filmcoopi), Turkey (Chantier) and the former Yugoslavia region (MCF).

	Distribution in France will be handled by Haut et Court, one of the film’s producers. 

	Directed by Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh – also known for “Gagarine” – the film will open this year’s Locarno’s Film Festival on Aug. 5, playing at Locarano’s Piazza Grande.
	

	“Fanny and Jérémy are among the most inspired and inspiring French filmmakers today, and Kinology couldn’t be happier to be part of their magnificent comeback after the wonderful ‘Gagarine’,” said its founder and CEO Grégoire Melin, noting their “unique blend of social and magical realism.”


	The film is produced by June Films and Haut et Court and co-produced by Les Films du Fleuve and Hobab.

	In “The Green Eyes,” Liatard and Trouilh follow little Chaya, who lives with her family in the Landes region in France. But when they learn they’re being evicted, her older brother Nour falls into a mysterious sleep.

	“We first learned about ‘resignation syndrome’ five years ago, through a photography exhibition featuring two sisters affected by this condition,” Liatard and Trouilh told Variety.

	“These little girls were sleeping side by side, locked in a deep sleep ever since their family’s request for asylum had been denied. Those images deeply moved us. When we realized that hundreds of children had been affected by this condition, we wondered what these young children, trapped in their sleep, were dreaming about. That was the starting point for our desire to tell a story from a child’s perspective and dive into the dreams of a little girl who will do everything she can to wake her big brother up.”
	

	Liatard and Trouilh decided to answer Variety’s questions together. 

	“We do everything together,” they admitted. 

	“We’ve been working as a directing duo for over 10 years now, and we feel lucky to be able to share this journey together. We still don’t divide up the work.” 

	Thorough research was important in order to address this disease in the film.

	“It truly exists, even if we then venture into the realms of fiction and magic. We met doctors who specialize in this disease and young people who have awakened from it, sometimes after several years of deep lethargy. These powerful testimonies conveyed to us the sheer strength of these children.” 

	They also inspired the resilience of Chaya and Nour’s.

	“In our story, Chaya never loses hope of saving her brother, and it is thanks to the love that binds them and the power of her imagination that she succeeds.”

	Douae Butarbuch M’Zaouki, Sayyid El Alami, Anamaria Vartolomei, Arcadi Radeff, Omar Al Jbaai star. 

	Liatard and Trouilh combined reality and fiction in their award-winning “Gagarine,” where a boy who wants to become an astronaut tries to save his home from demolition. 

	“We love to explore reality without being realistic! Diving into the imagination and our characters’ dreams allows us to explore their emotions in a very visual way.” 

	In “The Green Eyes,” the Landes forest, where they filmed, is already “magical in itself.” 

	“There’s this lighthouse standing in the middle of the pine forest, and a little village covered in sand. It’s a paradise for these children, but also the place where all their traumas are replayed,” they said. They also praised Guillaume Laurant (“Amélie,” “I Lost My Body”), who joined them as a screenwriter. 

	“He shared some of the magic of his vision with us.”

	“It’s always a major challenge for us to strike the right balance between realism and magical elements. On the one hand, it was important to ground the film in real everyday life, and the archive footage helps us connect with the reality of the syndrome. On the other hand, we wanted to delve into Chaya’s imagination until the boundary between dream and reality gradually blurred.”
	

	They enjoy focusing on younger protagonists who are not afraid to dream. 

	“Dreamers know no borders; they invent the worlds of their choice. These worlds are refugees, and when reality becomes too violent, they can serve as escape routes,” they noted. 

	“It’s true that children and teenagers often find it easier to immerse themselves in their imaginations. But it’s also the hearts of adult dreamers that we hope to reach.”

schema.headline: ‘Gagarine’ Directors Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh Talk ‘The Green Eyes’ as Kinology Announces First Sales: ‘Dreamers Know No Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Dominates U.K. and Ireland Box Office With Massive Launch
description: Sony’s superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” stormed to the top of the U.K. and Ireland box office, recording an opening frame of £36.4
body:
Sony’s superhero blockbuster “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” stormed to the top of the U.K. and Ireland box office, recording an opening frame of £36.4 million ($48.9 million). 

	The total marks the third-highest opening in U.K. history, trailing only “Avengers: Endgame” ($58.3 million) and “Spectre” ($55.5 million). Across its pure three-day weekend (Friday–Sunday), the web-slinger collected $31.5 million from 716 locations for a $44,056 site average – registering as the fourth-biggest weekend launch of all time behind “Endgame,” “Star Wars: The Force Awakens,” and “Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part 2.” 
	

	Universal’s “The Odyssey” moved to second place in its third weekend of release. Directed by Christopher Nolan, the epic feature added $9.1 million over the frame, driving its cumulative local gross to $67.7 million.


	Disney claimed the third position with Pixar’s “Toy Story 5,” which added $1.4 million in its seventh frame. The animated hit lifted its seven-week running total to $69.7 million. Universal’s “Minions & Monsters” followed in fourth place during its fifth weekend, taking $1 million for a cumulative total of $19.3 million.

	Disney’s live-action “Moana” finished fifth in its fourth week of release, collecting $967,566 to raise its running cume to $14 million. Black Bear’s ensemble comedy-drama “The Invite” occupied sixth place in its fifth weekend, banking $256,325 to push its cume to $4.6 million.

	Universal’s “Obsession” captured seventh place in its 12th frame, taking $187,276 for a total of $26 million. Studiocanal’s “Evil Dead Burn” held eighth spot in its fourth frame, adding $97,676 for a cume of $3.1 million.
	

	BFI Distribution entered the chart at ninth place with Imran Perretta’s Venice Critics’ Week selection “Ish,” which recorded an opening weekend of $41,900. Rounding out the top 10, TGS Cinemas Limited’s Indian political action feature “Jana Nayagan” added $35,449 in its sophomore session, bringing its total to $735,621.

	Looking ahead to the upcoming theatrical frame, Laverock Productions is releasing Ian Findlay’s agricultural documentary “A Dairy Story” and Dogwoof launching “David Byrne’s American Utopia” alongside CinemaLive’s event presentation “Turandot On Sydney Harbour – Opera Australia 2016. Also coming up is the music event release “Ateez: Light the Way in Cinemas.”

	Wide-circuit launches Include Paramount’s animated sequel “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” Warner Bros.’ fantasy revival “Practical Magic,” Disney’s comedy entry “Super Troopers 3” and Studiocanal’s horror title “Ice Cream Man.” 

	Releases also include Netflix’s drama “A Child of My Own,” Conic’s “The Summer Book,” Dreamz Entertainment’s Indian feature “Korean Kanakaraju,” Peccadillo Pictures’ drama “Love Me Tender,” Radiance Films’ classic title “Nadja,” and TAPE Collective’s “Bouchra.” 

	Archival and anniversary releases include Park Circus re-issuing Aardman’s animated comedy “Flushed Away” alongside Vertigo Releasing showcasing the 10th Anniversary restoration of Taika Waititi’s “Hunt For The Wilderpeople”. 

	Weekend event cinema offerings conclude with Piece Of Magic Entertainment presenting “Andre Rieu’s 2026 Summer Concert: Viva Maastricht!” and Trafalgar Releasing debuting “Grateful Dead Meet-Up At The Movies 2026.”

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Dominates U.K. and Ireland Box Office With Massive Launch

title: Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Singapore has never really had a wuxia feature film – though the genre was a fixture of local television in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when a w
body:
Singapore has never really had a wuxia feature film – though the genre was a fixture of local television in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when a wave of wuxia serials cast actors like Li Nanxing and Zhu Ming. 

	Nelson Yeo is closing that gap with “The House on the Moon,” a lunar reimagining of the Chang’Er myth landing in Locarno’s international competition. Variety is exclusively unveiling a clip from the film, ahead of its world premiere.
	

	Wuxia is the Chinese genre of sword-fighting heroes and martial fantasy that has powered everything from King Hu’s classics to Wong Kar-wai’s “Ashes of Time.”


	“It was quite ambitious when we first started having this idea of picking wuxia,” Yeo tells Variety. “For this one I decided to fully embrace genre and see where the film can take us.”

	Yeo has a habit of returning to Locarno. He attended the festival’s Filmmakers Academy in 2018, then premiered his 2023 debut feature, “Dreaming & Dying,” there, where it won the Filmmakers of the Present Golden Leopard and the Swatch First Feature Award. Three years on, he’s back for a third time.

	“I’m super glad to be back in Locarno,” Yeo says.

	The film reimagines the legend of Chang’Er, the moon goddess, and her husband, the archer Hou Yi, picking up the story after Chang’Er ascends to the moon and setting her on a journey to its dark side alongside a bandit from Earth. For Yeo, the appeal was less about honoring the myth than filling in what it leaves out.

	“The original myth has always been so simple,” Yeo says. “As a kid, you can pretty much recite the whole story in a couple of lines and people will get it. But then at the same time, you always wonder what are these characters really going through? What are their emotions like?”
	

	He points to Peng Meng, the disciple mentioned only in passing in the traditional tale, as the character who benefited most from that expansion. “It’s just a very basic foundation,” Yeo says. “So I felt like I have more, I can take more liberties in terms of like building the character.” Even so, he adds, the story remains centered on its heroine: “Chang’Er is traveling to the dark side of the moon throughout the film, but essentially, it’s about a journey inside herself and finding herself again and finding her own voice, in fact.”

	That affinity for late-1980s and 1990s wuxia runs deep. Yeo grew up on Hong Kong genre cinema and the wuxia television serials that were once a fixture of Singaporean TV, and he cites Tsui Hark’s “Zu: Warriors From the Magic Mountain” as a touchstone alongside Wong Kar-wai’s “Ashes of Time.” But reviving that language now came with practical headaches. “Sourcing for the props was a nightmare,” Yeo says. “And in terms of location wise, because Singapore being such a modern city, we had a lot of trouble finding proper locations to shoot the film.”

	Those constraints pushed part of the production to Taiwan, Yeo’s first time filming there. “It was quite an eye opener in terms of how things are done there,” he says. The Taiwan leg also brought him into the orbit of Lee Kang-sheng, the Taiwanese thespian and longtime Tsai Ming-liang regular, a collaboration Yeo calls a highlight of the production. “He’s amazing because he’s a one-take wonder,” Yeo says. “Everything that he does on the first day is just perfect. And I’m so fortunate to work with him.”

	The film’s tonal balance owes much to its bandit character, written to speak Singlish and cast, Yeo says, to give audiences an entry point among a story otherwise populated by immortals. “I really wanted that character to be the one that the audience can really relate to,” he says. “After all, he a mortal in among all these immortals. He’s the closest to the audience.” The role also reshaped the film’s register. “The original character that was written was much darker and the film was much darker,” Yeo says. “I felt like having this different element, this slightly more comedic character, lightens things up a little bit.”

	Shot partly through virtual production, “The House on the Moon” pushed Yeo toward tools he still regards with caution. “First and foremost, I feel like virtual production is a game changer,” he says. “At the same time, it’s not so accessible to independent filmmakers because of the inherent cost of it.” He’s warier still of artificial intelligence’s growing role in production. “Nothing beats being on the real locations, having the actors interact with the space,” Yeo says. “There’s so much more room for creative freedom on set in terms of blocking or improv. 
	

	Working with a cast and crew spanning Singapore, Taiwan and beyond, including a German visual effects team and an Indonesian composer based in Berlin, was, Yeo says, a deliberate widening of his usual process.

	As for what the film’s Locarno premiere means to him, Yeo would rather audiences approach it without a map. “I guess just to give in to their senses and not go in with any expectations,” he says. “The plot maybe on the surface it sounds really complicated, but as long as you follow the characters’ emotions, I think you’ll be fine.”

	Whether “The House on the Moon” spins off into a franchise remains an open question for Yeo. “If it happens, if it happens,” he says. “I won’t force it. I won’t force myself to make a sequel of the film.” He’s already looking elsewhere: a horror project he’s drafted, and “Black Sun,” a film he’s been trying to get made for more than a decade.

	“The House on the Moon” is produced by Tan Si En, Wendy Lie and Kuek Shee Heng for Momo Film Co (part of Fremantle), and Aview Images, in co-production with Weydemann Bros., 9LB Film, KawanKawan Media and Widewall Pictures. It is financed by the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA). The film’s proof of concept secured support from the VP Innovation Fund by Singapore’s IMDA.Parallax Films holds worldwide exclusive sales rights (excluding German speaking territories, Taiwan, and Singapore) and non-exclusive rights for all other regions in Southeast Asia.

	The film stars Lim Shi-An, Dominick Rustam, Harry Chang and Akira Huang, with a special appearance by Lee Kang-sheng.

title: Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Acclaimed Bengali cinema actor Parno Mittra is stepping behind the camera as a producer for the first time with “The Music Teacher,” a British-India
body:
Acclaimed Bengali cinema actor Parno Mittra is stepping behind the camera as a producer for the first time with “The Music Teacher,” a British-Indian short film starring Raima Sen that begins principal photography this month in Kolkata.

	The project is co-produced by Tabernacle Street Films (U.K.) and Unscripted Co (India), the production banner Mittra is launching with this film. Written and directed by Shrimoyee Chakraborty, “The Music Teacher” is her first Bengali narrative film, following her documentary “Spirit of the Wildflower” and her work as creator and presenter of “India Bites.” Chakraborty also produces for Tabernacle Street Films, alongside Mittra’s producing role for Unscripted Co. Editor Aarti Bajaj, known for her work on “Jab We Met,” “Rockstar,” “Highway,” “Tamasha,” “Sacred Games,” “Jubilee” and “Amar Singh Chamkila,” comes aboard as co-producer.
	

	Sen takes the title role, with Niranjan Mondal, who appeared in “Laughtersane,” rounding out the cast.


	Inspired by Chakraborty’s mother, “The Music Teacher” is set in North Kolkata and centers on a young man struggling with depression who finds a path back to life through a teacher of Rabindra Sangeet, the genre of songs composed by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore that remains central to Bengali culture. The film is billed as a tribute to Rabindra Sangeet and the educators who have preserved Bengal’s cultural heritage across generations, exploring resilience and human connection.

	Mittra has spent more than two decades building a career as one of Bengali cinema’s most established actors, with credits including “Doob (No Bed of Roses),” “Rajkahini,” “Apur Panchali” and “Ranjana Ami Ar Ashbona.” 
	

	“‘The Music Teacher’ embodies the kind of cinema I want Unscripted Co to champion – stories that are deeply rooted, emotionally resonant and capable of travelling across cultures,” Mittra said. “After more than two decades as an actor, producing this film marks an exciting new chapter in my creative journey. As our first production, this project represents the beginning of the vision I have for Unscripted Co, and I couldn’t have asked for a more inspiring team to bring it to life.”

	“‘The Music Teacher’ is my love letter to my mother, to Rabindra Sangeet and to Kolkata,” Chakraborty added. “It’s an incredibly personal story, and I’m honored to be making it alongside such an extraordinary team.”

	“I’ve spent my career helping shape stories in the edit room, and producing feels like a natural extension of that journey,” Bajaj said. “‘The Music Teacher’ is intimate, deeply moving and profoundly human. I’m delighted to come on board as co-producer and help bring Shrimoyee’s beautiful vision to the screen.”

schema.headline: Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Hyun Bin, Jung Woosung Collide Again as ‘Made in Korea’ Sets September Return on Disney+ and Hulu
description: “Made in Korea” will return for a second season on Sept. 9, streaming exclusively on Disney+ and Hulu, with stars Hyun Bin, Jung Woosung and Woo Doh
body:
“Made in Korea” will return for a second season on Sept. 9, streaming exclusively on Disney+ and Hulu, with stars Hyun Bin, Jung Woosung and Woo Dohwan reprising their roles for the six-episode continuation of the crime noir series.

	Season 2 picks up with Baek Kitae, played by Hyun Bin, still climbing toward power in the aftermath of framing prosecutor Jang Geonyoung. Now serving as deputy director within the Korean CIA, Kitae has grown his wealth and influence while expanding drug operations throughout the region. As political turmoil and public discontent grow, Geonyoung, played by Jung Woosung, emerges from the shadows to chase down a revenge plot nearly a decade in the making. The season sees both men escalate their tactics as they attempt to eliminate each other for good. Woo Dohwan returns as Baek Kihyun, Kitae’s brother.
	

	Season 2 is written by Park Eunkyo, who also wrote the first season along with credits including “The Silent Sea” and “Mother.” Woo Minho, director of the first season and of “The Man Standing Next” and “Inside Men,” returns to direct. Hive Media Corp, the company behind “Inside Men,” “The Man Standing Next” and “12.12: The Day,” produces.


	The season will launch with a two-episode premiere on Sept. 9, followed by two new episodes each Wednesday through Sept. 23.

	Season 1 of “Made in Korea” was 2025’s top-viewed Korean original series premiere on Disney+ within the Asia-Pacific region. That season followed Kitae as an ambitious KCIA agent leading a double life, working as a government operative by day while running an illegal smuggling operation by night. His rise up the ranks eventually brought him into conflict with Geonyoung, a prosecutor who refused to be bought off.
	

	Disney+ and Hulu’s Korean drama slate also includes “A Shop for Killers” seasons one and two, “The Manipulated,” about a man seeking revenge after being wrongly convicted of a crime, and “Tempest,” centered on a conspiracy that puts the Korean Peninsula’s stability at risk.

schema.headline: Hyun Bin, Jung Woosung Collide Again as ‘Made in Korea’ Sets September Return on Disney+ and Hulu

title: Shudder Nabs U.S. Rights to ‘Bloody Tennis’ and Horror Film Grabs Buyers in Other Major Territories Ahead of Locarno World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Nikias Chryssos‘ English-language horror film “Bloody Tennis” has secured several international deals, including to Shudder in the U.S., ahead of it
body:
Nikias Chryssos‘ English-language horror film “Bloody Tennis” has secured several international deals, including to Shudder in the U.S., ahead of its world premiere at the Locarno Film Festival.

	The other deals are for Australia (Umbrella Entertainment), Baltics (BestFilm.eu), Italy (Plaion Pictures), Japan (Extreme Film), Poland (9th Plan), and Scandinavia (Njutafilms).

	U.S. rights were handled by CAA on behalf of Augenschein Sales, while Augenschein Sales sold the Australian rights directly. The Playmaker Munich closed the deals for Poland, the Baltics, Japan, Scandinavia and Italy on behalf of Augenschein Sales, and is handling the remaining open territories.
	

	“Bloody Tennis” stars Sandra Guldberg Kampp (“Foundation”), Golden Globe nominee Helena Zengel (“News of the World,” “The Legend of Ochi”), Tracy Gotoas (“Safe House”), Lucie Zhang (“Paris,” “13th District”), Lily Taieb (“The French Dispatch,” “Bergman Island”), Elina Löwensohn (“Schindler’s List”) and Zlatko Burić (“Triangle of Sadness”).


	The score is by Jim Williams, known for “Titane,” “Raw” and “Possessor.”

	The film takes the world of elite sports to disturbing new extremes, filled with brutal ambition, blood-sucking leeches and hard-hitting serves. After being admitted to an elite tennis academy hidden deep in Southern Europe, Sophie (Guldberg Kampp) must contend not only with the fierce brutality of her teammates but with the school’s increasingly sinister undercurrents, where competitive sports are taken to their painful limits and only the hungriest survive.
	

	The film is produced by Jonas Katzenstein and Maximilian Leo (“The Weight,” “The Assessment,” “Mother Mary”) of Augenschein in co-production with Port au Prince Film & Kultur Produktion and ZDF. The film was shot in Gran Canaria, Spain and NRW, Germany, with Volcano Films having rendered the Spanish production services. The production was supported by Film-und Medienstiftung NRW and German Federal Film Fund (DFFF) as well as the tax incentive program of the Canary Islands. The German distributor will be Port au Prince. Its first release is set for the U.S. via Shudder.

	Adam Koehler, director, acquisitions and productions at IFC Entertainment Group, said, “ ‘Bloody Tennis’ serves up an unexpectedly wild ride that will keep viewers exhilarated from start to finish. Distinctive, elegant, and gleefully offbeat, it’s exactly the kind of bold, boundary-pushing horror we strive to champion at Shudder. We’re thrilled to give this unforgettable film a home on our platform.”

	Sylvia Edelmann, head of sales at The Playmaker Munich, said the world premiere in Locarno will give the film “the attention it deserves and help us showcase it to buyers in the remaining open territories.”

	Katzenstein said, “After years of hard work, we’re incredibly excited to finally bring ‘Bloody Tennis’ to audiences with its world premiere in Locarno. This film would not exist without the extraordinary vision of Nikias, our wonderful cast and the dedication of everyone involved. Knowing that it has already found partners in so many territories—and that it will begin its journey with Shudder in North America—makes this moment even more special. We can’t wait for audiences to finally enter the strange and unsettling world we have created together.”

	Chryssos is an alumnus of the Résidence du Festival de Cannes, the Berlinale Talents, the Saatchi & Saatchi New German Directors Showcase and the Masterclass “The Hollywood Perspective” at UCLA.

	In 2012, he founded the production company Kataskop Film, and produced and directed his first feature film, “Der Bunker,” in co-production with Geißendörfer Film, which premiered at the 65th Berlin Intl. Film Festival, and won the Next Wave Award for best feature at Fantastic Fest in Austin. His second feature film, “A Pure Place,” was developed in the Résidence du Festival de Cannes, and premiered at the Munich Film Festival, where it won the award for best director.

schema.headline: Shudder Nabs U.S. Rights to ‘Bloody Tennis’ and Horror Film Grabs Buyers in Other Major Territories Ahead of Locarno World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Tadanobu Asano, Yukino Kishii’s Cannes Title ‘All the Lovers in the Night’ Lands North American Distribution (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Bitters End has set North American distribution for “All the Lovers in the Night,” Yukiko Sode‘s Yukino Kishii and Tadanobu Asano starrer that premi
body:
Bitters End has set North American distribution for “All the Lovers in the Night,” Yukiko Sode‘s Yukino Kishii and Tadanobu Asano starrer that premiered in Un Certain Regard at Cannes earlier this year.

	Several Futures has acquired the film for the U.S. and Ritual Films for Canada. The company has also closed a deal with Movies Matter for Thailand.

	The new deals join a slate of previously announced territories, including France, where Art House Films will distribute the film after releasing Sode’s “Aristocrats,” which drew more than 71,000 admissions in the country. Additional territories include Spain (Atalante), Bulgaria (NeterraTV+), Brazil (Belas Artes Grupo), South Korea (Pancinema), Taiwan (Andrews Film), Hong Kong (Edko Films), Singapore (Anticipate Pictures) and Indonesia (PT Falcon).
	

	Based on Mieko Kawakami’s novel, the film follows Fuyuko, a freelance proofreader whose solitary existence shifts after she meets Mitsutsuka, a high school physics teacher, at a local culture center. Kishii plays Fuyuko, with Asano as Mitsutsuka.


	Kawakami’s novel became an international literary sensation, reaching English-language readers and more than a dozen other markets worldwide. It holds the distinction of being the first work of Japanese fiction to make the shortlist for the U.S. National Book Critics Circle Award.

	Sode both wrote and directed the film, working from Kawakami’s source material. Her previous feature “Aristocrats” bowed at the International Film Festival Rotterdam ahead of its French theatrical run. She also wrote and directed the Disney+ series “Because We Forget Everything” (2025).
	

	“I see this not as a story about the two of them, Fuyuko and Mitsutsuka, but as a portrait of a woman’s everyday life after she falls in love. She isn’t thinking about romance twenty-four hours a day, so by giving more time to moments that don’t involve Mitsutsuka, I felt we could more clearly convey the subtle shifts in her daily life,” Sode had told Variety ahead of the film’s Cannes premiere.

	Kishii previously earned international acclaim for her performance in Sho Miyake’s “Small, Slow But Steady,” which bowed at the Berlin Film Festival, won her the best actress award at the Japan Academy Film Prize. Asano’s role as Lord Kashigi Yabushige in FX’s “Shōgun” brought him a Golden Globe for best supporting actor on television, along with a Primetime Emmy nod – the first such nomination for a Japanese actor in that category.

	“All the Lovers in the Night” will open in Japan on Nov. 13.

schema.headline: Tadanobu Asano, Yukino Kishii’s Cannes Title ‘All the Lovers in the Night’ Lands North American Distribution (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Haugesund New Nordic Films Unveils French Focus Including a Case Study on ‘Ibelin,’ From ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum (EXCLUSIVE)
description: New Nordic Films, the Norwegian International Film Festival’s industry confab in Haugesund, has announced the program for its first ever French Focu
body:
New Nordic Films, the Norwegian International Film Festival’s industry confab in Haugesund, has announced the program for its first ever French Focus, set up to foster partnerships and co-productions between France and the Nordic countries.  The event, due to run Aug. 25-28, is organised by New Nordic Films in partnership with the Institut Francais de Norvège, the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs, France’s National Center for Cinema (CNC) and promotional body Unifrance.

	Headlining the French Focus is a pitching session on Aug. 26 at the Nordic Co-Production Market of four French films in development, of which two are produced by pedigreed producer Les Valseurs, a Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize winner this year for “Elephants in the Fog” and Un Certain Regard top prize winner in 2025 for “The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo.”Produced by Les Valseurs co-founder Damien Megherdi, “Borderline” is the feature length spin-off of Yves Piat’s Oscar and César nominated short film “Nefta Football Club,” while “All the Softness in the World” is an ambitious animation project by Turkish artist Ayçe Kartal whose short film “Wicked Girl” was the first animation short to scoop the Grand Prix in Clermont-Ferrand in 2018.
	

	Two other directorial debuts make the cut: the creative documentary “Boutès” by Jeanne Géli and Loïs Szymczak, produced by Womanray’s Marielle Tricoire, co-producer of Jim Jarmusch’s “Father Mother Sister Brother” and “Temporary Lives” by Syrian-Norwegian filmmaker Wessam Hachicho, produced by Respiro Productions (“In the Nguyen Kitchen”).  

	Besides the four-title pitch, the French Focus will include a panel on co-production opportunities between France and the five Nordic countries, and a case study on the anticipated “Ibelin” by Norwegian-born Morten Tyldum, mostly famed for the Oscar-winning “The Imitation Game.” The biopic about online gamer Mats Steen – starring Charlie Plummer, Stephen Graham, Toni Collette, and Bill Nighy – is currently in production for France’s Vendôme Pictures, Pathé, and Norway’s Neby-Tyldum AS. 

	“I am incredibly happy that we are finally able to have a French focus in Haugesund,” said Gyda Velvin Myklebust, head of New Nordic Films. “French cinema is well-known internationally for high artistic quality, and we in the Nordic region have also recently made a strong mark internationally,” she added, referring to “Sentimental Value”’s Oscar win for Best International Feature, the first ever for Norway. “France and the Nordics have highly talented and ambitious filmmakers, and we believe our French focus will give wind to a French-Nordic wave of co-productions and creative collaborations between our countries.”
	

	For Kjersti Mo, CEO at the Norwegian Film Institute (NFI) the French Focus reflects “a growing recognition that European film depends on stronger international collaboration.”

	“France has one of Europe’s strongest film cultures and most developed production ecosystems, while the Nordic countries bring distinctive stories, strong creative talent and considerable international experience,” Mo added. “These different strengths are precisely what can make the partnerships valuable,” said the NFI chief, who also underscored that  “international collaboration is a central priority” in the institute’s new strategy.Speaking to Variety, Michel Plazanet, CNC director of international affairs, pointed out that “the Nordic countries, which traditionally co-produce extensively among themselves, are now “seeking additional partners, particularly in France, as this opens up numerous opportunities: access to funding (such as “Aide aux Cinémas du Monde,” regional co-production funds, Arte, and SOFICA), distribution advantages (French sales agents have an excellent reputation, and French co-productions gain easier access to the Cannes and Annecy festivals), and better access to the French theatrical market, the largest in Europe, especially for arthouse cinema.”

	Conversely the Nordics offer clear advantages for French producers, Plazanet said, as the region boasts “robust institutions, substantial and diverse public and private funding, and reliable professionals accustomed to international co-production.”

	Aide au Cinéma du Monde

	So far 20 Nordic projects have received backing from the ACM including three Cannes entries from Joachim Trier (“Sentimental Value,” “The Worst Person in the World,” “Louder than Bombs”), and two from Tarik Saleh (“Eagles of the Republic,” Boys from Heaven”).
	

	Denmark, Norway, and Sweden are the most active [co-production] countries, but Iceland also performs very well, given its very small population,” Plazanet said.Among the French Focus attendees, Julie Billy, founder of Paris-based June Films, was just granted ACM support for the Icelandic project in production “A Favour” by Grímur Hákonarson (“Rams”), and is developing a project with Norway’s Eye Eye Pictures (“Fjord,” “Sentimental Value”). “The French Focus comes at exactly the right moment,” said the producer, also interested in creators – notably from the Sámi community, “whose perspectives are unique and increasingly important on the international scene.”“I would love to see Norway as a minority co-producer in more French productions, and of course the other way around,” added Eye Eye Pictures co-founder Andrea Berendsen Ottmar who also hopes the French Focus will “inspire, so that we can help each other to think outside the box in terms of how we structure and finance our projects. Independent producers all over Europe need to stand together and support each other, and forums like this are very valuable in that sense,” she observed.As noted by Plazanet, the French Focus plays within a series of French/Nordic industry events, multiplied in the last two years, that peaked in 2025 with the Visions Nordiques Festival in Paris. Next on the CNC’s top agenda is “an institutional alignment on key European issues, notably the transposition of the AVMS Directive and platform obligations.”

	The Norwegian International Film festival, running Aug. 22-28, will platform eight French films in its section French Touch. 

	Drilling down on the four French projects lined-up for the Nordic Co-Production Market

	“Bordeline” (“Sur la ligne,” Yves Piat)Produced by Daniel Megherbi, Les Valseurs

	Feature debut from the director of the 2020 Oscar-nominated short film “Neftah Football Club who has sketched out ideas from his short, together with writer Alaa Eddine Aljem (“The Unknown Saint”). The story turns Hishem, on a customs officer on the Algerian-Tunisian border, who encounters Tesla, a donkey lost in the desert with headphones over his ears, with a bag of cocaine on his back. 

	Producer Megherbi who co-produced with the Nordics Nepalese pic “Elephants in the Fog,” a Cannes’ Jury Prize winner, believes “Bordeline”’s deadpan, absurd humor, “somewhere between Elia Suleiman and the Coen brothers,” will resonate well with Nordic partners and the general audience. Public backers on board include the CNC, Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine and ICEC in Spain via Spanish co-producers Sumendi and BTeam Pictures. Filming is pencilled for April-May 2027. 

	“All the Softness in the World” (“Toute la douceur du monde,” Ayçe Kartal)Produced by Damien Megherbi, Les Valseurs

	Turkish animation filmmaker Ayçe Kartal and Megherbi reunite on the helmer’s feature length debut after his multi-awarded short film “Wicked Girls,” an Annecy Jury Prize) winner. Set in 1950, the story follows the young Levon who has grown up posing as a girl, to be protected from an ancient family vendetta. In his search for his true identity, Levon lands in Paris in the world of Haute Couture where he begins to recover a sense of self through creativity. 

	“I want to explore, through [Levon] an alternative history of fashion, one rooted in survival, not spectacle,” said Kartal in a statement. “At Haugesund, we hope to find a Nordic co-producer who understands what we’re trying to achieve with this project. It’s an ambitious, innovative piece of adult animation, and we want a partner who’s genuinely excited by that,” said Megherbi who’s secured development support from the CNC and Hauts-de-France region.“Boutès” (Jeanne Géli, Loïs Szymczak)Produced by Marieke Tricoire, Womanray
	

	A liife-affirming documentary in which forensic pathologist Jeanne Géli turns filmmaker to capture the frailty and beauty of life, as her partner Loic Szymczak, an Olympic diver and visual artist, suddenly fights for his own life, upended by a malignant brain tumor. Together they move towards one act of faith-a performative dive in the heart of Paris. 

	“This film is, above all, a love story. We are making it to transform the reality of illness into poetic material,” said the co-directors. 

	Womanray founder Tricoire, who bridges luxury brands with film and served as co-producer on Jim Jarmusch’s Golden Lion winner “Father, Mother, Sister, Brother,” said she signed up for New Nordic Films when she found out that the founder of the extreme sport Døds diving (Death diving) was born in Norway. The project co-produced with Hutong in France, is currently shooting, with a delivery pencilled for 2028. “Temporary Lives” (Wessam Hachicho)Produced by Amélie Quéret, Respiro Productions

	Wessam Hachicho, a graduate from Oslo’s Westerdals film school and a former cinematographer in Syria, draws from her own uprooting experience to tell the story of a Syrian teenager refugee in Oslo and his estranged father as they seek asylum in Norway. “Beneath the [film’s] political context lies an intimate story about unresolved trauma, family bonds and the sacrifices parents and children make for one another,” said Hachicho. The film also asks how institutions shape individual lives, as every decision the characters make becomes a negotiation between survival, dignity, and hope.”

	Queret, who met the rising filmmaker at the Less is More Lab, said she was blown away by Hachicho’s script and “clear artistic identity.” In Haugesund, she will be looking for a Norwegian co-producer and access to Nordic funds. Filming is due to start in 2027.

title: Hwang Bo-reum, Lee Geum-yi Among Authors in Busan Story Market’s 2026 Selections
description: The Busan Story Market (BSM) has unveiled 25 official selections for 2026, including international bestseller Hwang Bo-reum and two-time Hans Christ
body:
The Busan Story Market (BSM) has unveiled 25 official selections for 2026, including international bestseller Hwang Bo-reum and two-time Hans Christian Andersen Award finalist Lee Geum-yi, drawing on original IP from four Asian countries.

	BSM is part of the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the official market of the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Among the Korean selections is “My Upstairs Neighbors” by Hwang Bo-reum, the author behind the international bestseller “Welcome to the Hyunam-dong Bookshop,” and “Chasm of Sorrow” by Lee Geum-yi, whose more than 50 published books and international translations have made her one of Korea’s most recognized children’s and young-adult authors. The lineup as a whole comprises 15 titles from Korea and four each from Taiwan and Japan, alongside two from Indonesia.
	

	Genres and narratives range widely this year, spanning stories that explore universal emotions and relationships, including life and death, family, growth, love and loss, through fresh genre settings, alongside plot-driven works built around hidden agendas and fixations that take unpredictable turns.


	BSM operates as a marketplace connecting film and audiovisual adaptations of original IP, drawing from books, webtoons, web novels, video games and other formats, with content platforms and IP holders worldwide. The official selections take part in pitching sessions and one-on-one business meetings aimed at secondary rights deals and adaptation collaborations.

	For the Korean IP selection, BSM fielded 138 submissions from 83 companies this year, ultimately choosing 15 titles from 13 companies: nine books, two webtoons, two web novels and two stories. Books make up more than half the Korean lineup, though the selections stay broadly balanced across formats and genres. The titles pair crowd-pleasing categories, among them romance, mystery, fantasy and family drama, with less conventional hooks, including parallel worlds, out-of-body experiences and science fiction, touching on themes from generational communication and family bonds to individual lives set against their times. The selection ranges from emotionally driven human dramas to AI-inflected fantasy, genre-blending historical romance, period pieces and hybrid concepts.
	

	BSM’s Taiwanese IP selection, conducted annually with the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), yielded four titles from four companies, one apiece drawn from books, webtoons, web novels and comics. Each centers on a high concept distinctive enough to convey its identity in a single line, using fantasy settings not merely for spectacle but to work through emotional terrain that includes bereavement, remorse, early romance, ties between family members and coming of age, positioning the titles for adaptation across film, drama series and other formats.

	Four Japanese IPs from four companies, one book and three comics, were chosen through the Visual Industry Promotion Organization (VIPO). The selections lean on layered characters and relationships built around secrets and obsessions, with stories shifting in unpredictable directions as hidden truths surface or unlikely individuals form bonds across boundaries.

	Indonesia’s two selections, both comics from two separate companies, were picked from a shortlist of 10 Indonesian original IPs that had been presented at the 2025 JAFF Content Market, an initiative run by the Jogja-NETPAC Asian Film Festival Market (JAFF Market); the pair emerged after a round of pitches and meetings centered on adapting the properties for film and audiovisual formats. Both took home the JAFF Content Market Award Goes to ACFM 2026, earning them a spot in this year’s BSM lineup. JAFF Content Market has since evolved into JAFF IP Connection for 2026, and one of BSM’s selected Korean IPs will be invited to that program following talks with JAFF Market representatives. The Yogyakarta, Indonesia program runs Nov. 28-30, continuing the two-way exchange of original IP between BSM and JAFF Market.

	BSM runs alongside APM at ACFM, which takes over Exhibition Center 2 at BEXCO in Busan for four days starting Oct. 10, with the 25 selections set to connect with industry professionals through BSM Pitch & Match sessions and further business meetings exploring IP expansion and adaptation opportunities.

	ACFM is the official market of BIFF and is held in Busan every October. The 2025 edition, ACFM’s 20th, drew industry professionals from 55 countries – 3,024 of them, alongside 1,222 registered companies – with on-site attendance reaching a record 30,006. The Sales Market tallied 8,438 business meetings, generating an estimated $71.1 million in transactions.
	

	The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with the 21st ACFM held Oct. 10-13.

title: Ariana Grande Clarifies Break Was Planned, Says She Needed Boundaries
description:
Ariana Grande
                          I Needed Boundaries ...
                          Tour Is
body:
Ariana Grande
                          I Needed Boundaries ...
                          Tour Is Still 'Greatest' Experience!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 3, 2026
                            8:34 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Ariana Grande is clarifying the reason behind her upcoming break ... saying the decision was made long ago and wasn't an impulsive reaction to recent headlines.
      
    
            The singer addressed fans Monday night during her "Eternal Sunshine Tour" stop at Chicago's United Center, explaining she wanted to speak directly because stories that don't come from her can sometimes get blown out of proportion.
      
    
      
      ARIANA ADDRESSED EVERYTHING JUST NOW CHICAGO N1 pic.twitter.com/bciu6iOIo6
              @wfysaturnreturn
          
  
    
            Ariana said she had quietly planned the break well before it was announced and made the decision from a thoughtful and empowered place.
      
    
            She also clarified that while ongoing public scrutiny played a role in her need to set boundaries and step back, the negativity has not ruined the touring experience for her.
      

            Ariana explained that multiple things can be true at once ... she can need a break and stronger boundaries while still considering the tour the greatest experience of her professional and creative life.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The Grammy winner reassured fans who worried the criticism had overshadowed the experience, saying nothing happening outside the shows could outweigh the connection she shares with them or the joy she gets from making art with people she loves and respects.
      
    
            She described the tour as healing, beautiful and deeply meaningful, making clear she doesn't view her decision to step away as a rejection of this chapter of her career.
      
    
            Ariana plans to take a break from public facing work after wrapping the "Eternal Sunshine Tour," with her team pointing to the ongoing nature of the public scrutiny she's faced.
      
    
            Her message Monday was not that the criticism played no part in the decision ... but that it hasn't taken away from what the tour and her fans have meant to her.

title: Mary Rivera, 'Spider-Man: No Way Home' Actress, Dead at 82
description:
'Spider-Man: No Way Home'
                          Actress Mary Rivera Dead at 82
body:
'Spider-Man: No Way Home'
                          Actress Mary Rivera Dead at 82
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 3, 2026
                            5:01 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mary Rivera, who played Ned Leeds' Filipino grandmother in "Spider-Man: No Way Home," has died ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            A family member tells TMZ ... Mary suffered a stroke and doctors warned the family her condition was extremely serious. The relative says doctors told them even if Mary emerged from the coma, her prognosis would not be good, so the family made the difficult decision to remove her from life support.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Mary passed away April 15 in Honolulu. We're told the actress was later cremated.
      

            The family member tells us Mary lived a good life and was extremely proud of appearing in the 2021 Marvel blockbuster. Her family encouraged her to audition for the role, which ultimately became one of her proudest accomplishments.
      
    
            In one of the movie’s memorable scenes, she asks Andrew Garfield's Spider-Man to clean cobwebs from the ceiling while speaking in Tagalog as Ned translates.
      
    
            She is survived by her husband, Alejandro, her children, 11 grandchildren, and four great-grandchildren.
      
    
            Mary was 82.
      
    
            RIP.

title: Gigi Hadid and Bradley Cooper Wear Matching Rings, Spark Marriage Rumors
description:
Gigi Hadid & Bradley Cooper
                          Are Those Wedding Rings?!?
body:
Gigi Hadid & Bradley Cooper
                          Are Those Wedding Rings?!?
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It looks like Gigi Hadid and Bradley Cooper might've quietly gotten married ... because they stepped out wearing matching rings on THAT finger!!!
      
    
            Check out these photos ... the lovebirds were snapped in Paris on Monday, rocking bands on their left hands ... and holding hands. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Bradley and Gigi couldn't have been more laid back about the seemingly big reveal -- they were both rocking workout gear along with those rings.
      

            The exciting accessories come almost 3 years into their relationship ... they first stepped out together back in October 2023.
      
    
            BC and GH wouldn't be the first A-list couple to tie the knot in secret. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tom Holland and Zendaya still haven't officially said whether or not they're married ... although all signs point to yes!
      
    
            Who knows ... maybe grandiose, star-studded weddings are out and secret ceremonies are the hot trend now. 
      
    
            Either way, Bradley and Gigi make quite the cute couple!
